title: Potentially traumatic experiences and subsequent psychopathological symptoms in children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus.
summary:
Children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes often suffer from psychological stress and comorbid mental illness. 
It has not yet been sufficiently well investigated how often children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes have various stressful experiences and subsequently develop psychological stress symptoms (e.g. intrusive memories, sleep disorders or negative thoughts). Furthermore, it is unclear to what extent complications that can occur in the context of diabetes (e.g. severe hypoglycaemia) are also related to these psychological stress symptoms.

This pilot study examines pediatric and adolescent patients with type 1 diabetes who are treated in a specialized diabetes outpatient clinic using a questionnaire to determine how often they have experienced various stressful experiences and how severely they are affected by subsequent psychological stress symptoms.  In addition, long-term blood glucose levels and the experience of typical diabetes complications are also recorded.

The aim of this pilot study is to investigate the following questions, among others:
1. How often do children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes experience various stressful experiences?
2. How often do they develop psychological stress symptoms following such experiences?
3. Is there an association between the stress experienced and the psychological stress symptoms and long-term blood glucose? 
4. Is there an association between the experience of diabetes-typical complications and psychological stress symptoms? 
5. Do patients with high psychological stress symptoms differ from patients without high stress symptoms with regard to their long-term blood glucose?
conditions: Type 1 diabetes mellitus without complications controlled
Type 1 diabetes mellitus without complications: Uncontrolled

interventions.name: Patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus aged between 10 and 17 years with clinically relevant posttraumatic stress symptoms
Patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus aged between 10 and 17 years without clinically relevant posttraumatic stress symptoms

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- diagnosis of diabetes mellitus type 1 (ICD-10 E10.90 or E10.91)
Exclusion criteria:
- Reading and spelling disorder (ICD-10 F81.0)
- Dyslexia (ICD-10 R48.0)
- Severely below-average cognitive performance (according to cognitive performance diagnostics or clinical impression)
